children: Australia's 2Q GDP data due Wednesday could be a further impetus for the Reserve Bank of Australia to raise interest rates before the end of the year. Growth itself should be tepid, but the numbers also include wages and demand data that the RBA looks at closely. George Tharenou, chief economist at UBS, says he will review his forecast for a further rate increase after the data. For now, he's calling a hike in November, but says the risk of an earlier increase this month is material. Simply, inflation remains too high, he adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
